title: implement-incident-aware-pager-windows-and-signal-debouncing
creator: Ava Chen
description: After the capacity regression on 2025-02-07 we saw recurring burn-rate noise that generated noisy paging for mid-tier services. This ticket implements an incident-aware pager window and signal debouncing layer to reduce duplicates and transient burn pages while preserving rapid escalation for high-severity regressions. The scope covers: 1) a short-term debounce middleware for burn-rate alerts deployed to alerting pipeline; 2) a stateful ‘incident window’ that extends suppression for alerts tied to a known capacity incident; 3) documentation and dashboarding so oncall can understand suppressed signals; 4) unit and integration tests to validate no blind spots for true regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Burn-rate pages for the mid-tier group drop by >=60% on steady-state noise in two-week A/B test vs baseline
No increase in time-to-detect for high-severity SLO breaches (>=99th percentile latency alerts) measured across last-3 incidents
Suppression decisions are visible in the Console with a per-alert badge and suppression_reason field
Playbook updated with instructions for manual override and re-enable of suppressed signals
action_items: Implement debounce logic: require sustained burn-rate > threshold for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (configurable) - ENG
Add incident-tag propagation: when an incident is declared, mark related signals and extend suppression windows - ENG
Create Console UI indicators for suppressed alerts with link to incident doc - DES/PM
Add signal-level metadata to alert events (suppressed_by, suppression_window_end, associated_incident) - ENG
Run A/B test on 10% of production alert traffic for 2 weeks and measure pages/ton - ENG
Add automated smoke tests that simulate rapid transient burn spikes to verify debounce - ENG
Draft runbook update and oncall training notes; schedule 30-min walkthrough - PM/SRE

risks: Over-suppression could hide genuine regressions if thresholds mis-configured
Operational complexity: incident tagging requires reliable incident lifecycle events from PagerDuty/Incident Manager
UX confusion if suppression reasons are not prominently displayed to oncall
test_plan: Unit tests for debounce state transitions and threshold edge-cases - ENG
Integration test that injects alert events and validates suppression metadata is propagated to Console - ENG
Canary A/B test on 10% traffic for 2 weeks; monitor pages, MTTA, and false-negative rate - ENG/SRE
Post-deploy retrospective checklist to validate metrics and rollback if MTTA regresses beyond 5%
notes: This effort intentionally splits immediate mitigation (debounce middleware) from longer-term policy work (dynamic thresholds per service profile).
We will not change burn-rate thresholds in this ticket; threshold tuning will be a follow-up after we have suppression telemetry.
Estimated rollout window aims to avoid major deployments the week before critical enterprise demos in late March.
